subject: Pathology
vignette: A 24-year-old man sustains a superficial abrasion on his forearm while mountain biking. Twelve hours later the area is bright red, warm to the touch, and tender, and he has no fever. A physician explains that these findings reflect the vascular response of acute inflammation.
question: Which of the following mechanisms most directly produces the redness and warmth at this site?

options.text: Contraction of endothelial cells that opens interendothelial junctions in postcapillary venules
Relaxation of arteriolar smooth muscle with increased local blood flow
Sensitization of sensory nerve endings by bradykinin and prostaglandin E2
Directed migration of neutrophils along a C5a concentration gradient
Leakage of protein-rich fluid that raises interstitial oncotic pressure

explanation_correct: Rubor (redness) and calor (warmth) result from vasodilation, meaning relaxation of arteriolar smooth muscle, which increases blood flow to the injured area. Histamine, prostaglandins, bradykinin, and nitric oxide mediate this vasodilation. The same response slows flow and produces the stasis that later allows leukocytes to marginate along the vessel wall. The cardinal signs of inflammation are taught as matched pairs, and redness with warmth is the vasodilation pair.

explanation_incorrect.A: Endothelial contraction opens interendothelial junctions and increases vascular permeability, which produces the swelling (tumor) of inflammation rather than its redness and warmth.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sensitization of sensory nerve endings is the mechanism of dolor (pain); bradykinin, prostaglandin E2, and histamine are the mediators named for pain, not for redness.
explanation_incorrect.D: Chemoattraction of neutrophils toward C5a is the final migration step of leukocyte extravasation and does not change local blood flow or skin temperature.
explanation_incorrect.E: Protein-rich exudate leaking into the interstitium raises interstitial oncotic pressure and causes edema, which is swelling rather than erythema or warmth.

educationalObjective: Rubor and calor of acute inflammation are produced by arteriolar vasodilation, mediated by histamine, prostaglandins, bradykinin, and nitric oxide.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 31-year-old woman is stung by a bee on the dorsum of the hand. Within 20 minutes the site is swollen, tense, and indurated, and the swelling extends into the loose tissue of the fingers. Ultrasound shows increased fluid in the subcutaneous space with a high protein content.
question: Which of the following best explains the swelling in this lesion?

options.text: Arteriolar vasodilation raises capillary hydrostatic pressure while permeability remains unchanged
Obstruction of lymphatic channels by fibrin produces a low-protein transudate
Endothelial cell contraction opens interendothelial junctions, allowing protein-rich fluid to escape from postcapillary venules and raising interstitial oncotic pressure
Neutrophil proteases degrade interstitial collagen and reduce tissue turgor
Histamine-induced relaxation of arteriolar smooth muscle increases blood flow to the area

explanation_correct: Tumor (swelling) in acute inflammation is caused by increased vascular permeability. Endothelial contraction, for example after direct tissue damage, opens interendothelial junctions in postcapillary venules, so protein-rich fluid leaks into the interstitium as an exudate and raises interstitial oncotic pressure, drawing more water out of the vessel. Leukotrienes C4, D4, and E4, histamine, serotonin, and bradykinin all drive this endothelial contraction. A protein-rich exudate is the feature that separates this process from a hydrostatic transudate, and it is the reason the swelling here is tense and indurated.

explanation_incorrect.A: Raising capillary hydrostatic pressure without a change in permeability produces a transudate, as in heart failure; the protein-rich fluid described here indicates a permeability defect.
explanation_incorrect.B: Lymphatic obstruction does cause edema, but the fluid is a low-protein transudate and it does not explain the acute, localized, protein-rich swelling after a sting.
explanation_incorrect.D: Neutrophil proteases contribute to tissue damage in prolonged inflammation but do not generate the rapid protein-rich edema of the immediate response.
explanation_incorrect.E: Arteriolar relaxation explains the redness and warmth of the lesion, not the accumulation of protein-rich interstitial fluid.

educationalObjective: Swelling in acute inflammation reflects endothelial contraction with increased permeability and leakage of protein-rich exudate from postcapillary venules.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 30-year-old man with a 3-day history of fever, pleuritic chest pain, and a right lower lobe infiltrate has a diagnostic thoracentesis. A second patient, a 70-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy and bilateral effusions, has fluid drained for comparison. The laboratory reports protein content and specific gravity for both specimens.
question: Which of the following findings best identifies the fluid from the patient with pneumonia as an exudate?

options.text: Total protein of 1.5 g/dL with a specific gravity of 1.008
A glucose concentration equal to the serum glucose concentration
A red blood cell count of 500 cells per microliter
Total protein above 3 g/dL with a specific gravity above 1.020

explanation_correct: An exudate is the protein-rich fluid produced when increased vascular permeability lets plasma proteins cross the endothelium, which is why it has a high protein content (roughly above 3 g/dL) and a high specific gravity (roughly above 1.020). Permeability rises because endothelial contraction widens interendothelial junctions in postcapillary venules during inflammation. A transudate instead reflects a hydrostatic or oncotic imbalance across an intact endothelium, so it is protein-poor. This protein-based distinction is the bedside translation of the exudate versus transudate concept in acute inflammation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Low protein with a low specific gravity describes a transudate, the pattern expected with the cardiomyopathy patient rather than the one with pneumonia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glucose equal to serum glucose is typical of uncomplicated transudates and many exudates alike, so it does not separate the two categories the way protein content does.
explanation_incorrect.C: A modest red cell count can follow a traumatic tap or accompany inflammation and is not the defining feature of an exudate.
explanation_incorrect.D: A low fluid-to-serum protein ratio is characteristic of a transudate; exudative fluid has a high ratio.

educationalObjective: Exudates are protein-rich fluids produced by increased vascular permeability, whereas transudates are protein-poor fluids caused by hydrostatic or oncotic imbalance.
